summary: A laid-off worker who finds full-time work again is about as likely to be paid less than before as to be paid the same or more.
realLife: The 2026 displaced-workers survey found about 49 percent of reemployed full-time workers earned as much or more than on the lost job, down from about 62 percent two years earlier.
sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Worker Displacement news release: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/disp.nr0.htm
inGame: job record (pay) before and after the job-ended event.

turns.summary: The new employer pays more because the worker's skills were scarce.
turns.writesBack: new job record with higher pay; mood: relieved

turns.summary: The worker accepts lower pay and hides it from friends.
turns.writesBack: new job record with lower pay; tie to a close friend stays distant

turns.summary: The worker tells the household plainly and they cut spending together.
